notes: Actual results for calendar year 2024, as the town reported them in its Municipal Financial Report to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Walworth County.
Wisconsin towns govern the rural areas outside cities and villages; cities and villages are separate from the town around them.
Governmental funds are reported by function. Water, sewer, electric and other utility and enterprise funds are reported only as total revenues and expenses, counted as utility charges and utilities.
General government, conservation and development, and other spending count as overhead.
Debt is general obligation debt outstanding at year end, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Wisconsin local candidates file campaign finance reports with their municipal clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Wisconsin yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
